The '''2026 Adur District Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day, to elect 14 of 29 members of [[Adur District Council]] in [[West Sussex]], [[England]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=mhclgpress |date=2026-02-16 |title=Update on May 2026 local authority elections – MHCLG in the Media |url=https://mhclgmedia.blog.gov.uk/2026/02/16/update-on-may-2026-local-authority-elections/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=mhclgmedia.blog.gov.uk |language=en}}</ref>

==Summary==

===Background===
In [[2024 Adur District Council election|2024]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] won majority control of the council.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Adur result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000223 |access-date=2026-02-17 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> In January 2026, the council asked for the election to be postponed pending local government reorganisation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-20 |title=Councils support election delay to focus on major local restructure |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/25771730.worthing-adur-councils-back-local-election-delay/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=The Argus |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-01-09 |title=Will Sussex get to vote in 2026 or will elections be called off? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cn567we03v1o |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> However it was rescheduled on 16 February 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-16 |title=Elections back on across Sussex after government U-turn |url=https://www.brightonandhovenews.org/2026/02/16/elections-back-on-across-sussex-after-government-u-turn/ |access-date=2026-02-17 |website=Brighton and Hove News |language=en-US}}</ref>

Changes 2024–2026:
*July 2024: Steve Neocleous (Conservative) leaves party to sit as an independent<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boothroyd |first1=David |title=Three Rivers Lib Dems are two down |url=https://www.localcouncils.co.uk/2024/07/three-rivers-lib-dems-are-two-down/ |website=LocalCouncils.co.uk |access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>
*April 2025: Nigel Jenner (Labour) dies – by-election held June 2025<ref>{{cite news |last1=Le Duc |first1=Frank |title=Tributes paid after sudden death of councillor and former youth worker |url=https://www.brightonandhovenews.org/2025/04/05/tributes-paid-after-sudden-death-of-councillor-and-former-youth-worker/ |access-date=21 February 2026 |work=Brighton and Hove News |date=5 April 2025}}</ref>
*June 2025: Kate Davis (Labour) wins by-election<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Buckingham Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/5287/#2025-06-19 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>
*November 2025: Paul Mansfield (Conservative) leaves party to sit as an independent<ref>{{cite web |last1=Boothoryd |first1=David |title=Greens Wincheap from Lib Dems |url=https://www.localcouncils.co.uk/2025/11/greens-wincheap-from-lib-dems/ |website=LocalCouncils.co.uk |access-date=21 February 2026}}</ref>
*February 2026: Andy McGreggor, Neil Parkin, Carson Albury and Carol Albury leave the Conservative Party, and try to defect to Reform, but are refused entry. They subsequently sit as independents. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-26 |title=Tory councillors who quit party rejected by Reform |url=https://www.theargus.co.uk/news/25891741.west-sussex-tory-councillors-quit-party-rejected-reform/ |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=The Argus |language=en}}</ref>
